claim: Fujimoto, Meger, and Precup decompose offline (batch) deep RL extrapolation error into three named causes: absent data, model bias, and training mismatch.
stance_target: existence of a named, decomposed mechanism (not a single elimination) for offline value-learning failure
scope_conditions: Off-policy deep Q-learning / actor-critic methods trained on a fixed batch
quoted_support: "Absent Data. If any state-action pair (s, a) is unavailable, then error is introduced as some function of the amount of similar data and approximation error."

claim: The paper demonstrates extrapolation error positively via a graded battery of three dataset-construction protocols (final buffer, concurrent, imitation) that vary the distributional mismatch between the batch and the evaluation policy, showing the DDPG value estimate diverges (to 10^4-10^5 scale) as mismatch increases.
stance_target: a graded dose-response methodology as the template for converting single-arm eliminations into a positive mechanism demonstration
scope_conditions: Hopper-v1 continuous control, DDPG agent, three batch-generation protocols
quoted_support: "These experiments show extrapolation error can be highly problematic"

claim: In deterministic finite MDPs, extrapolation error can be formally decomposed via a Bellman-like recursive equation in terms of the divergence between the true and batch-empirical transition distributions, and batch-constrained Q-learning is proven to converge to the optimal value function under the batch-induced MDP.
stance_target: the feasibility of a formal, provable characterization of offline value-estimation error as a template for the offline-MBO paper's own diagnosis
scope_conditions: Deterministic, finite (tabular) MDPs only; the continuous/deep-network experiments are empirical, not covered by this formal result
quoted_support: "Theorem 1. Performing Q-learning by sampling from a batch B converges to the optimal value function under the MDP M_B."
